provenance.dataset_name: LOLA 5 m/pix south-pole site model: Connecting ridge (Site01)
provenance.citation: Barker, M. K., et al. (2021). Improved LOLA elevation maps for south pole landing sites: Error estimates and their impact on illumination conditions. Planetary and Space Science, 203, 105119. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.pss.2020.105119
provenance.vertical_unit: metres (as stored in the source raster)

methods.slope: Horn (1981) 3x3 finite difference on a metric grid; degrees from horizontal.
methods.rms_slope: arctan of the root-mean-square of tan(slope).
methods.roughness_rms_height: RMS of elevation after subtracting the 5x5-cell moving mean, over the same window.
methods.relief: Maximum minus minimum elevation in a square moving window.
methods.aggregation: Coarser scales are area averages of the working grid; no scale is finer than the source.
methods.coverage: Fraction of grid cells with a valid elevation; voids are never filled.

limitations: Remote-sensing terrain metrics cannot establish soil strength, wheel traction, or field safety.
Source data has a native pixel size of about 5 m.
Features smaller than the analysis scale (rocks, small craters, ruts) are not resolved.
Metrics are only comparable between sites when computed at the same scale.
Surface heights fill pixels with no laser return by interpolation; the counts product shows where.
Interpolated areas are smoother than the real surface, which lowers slope and roughness there.
5 m pixels do not resolve rover-scale rocks or small craters.
